problemStatement.plain: How hard is it to compute Kolmogorov-Arnold superposition representations? Hilbert13GeneralSpaces.lean formalizes the compact-metric-space superposition framework and records the effective computation problem as open because the classical proof is nonconstructive.

open: Given a compact metric space presented by finite approximations and a continuous function f : X -> R, determine the computational complexity of producing a Kolmogorov-Arnold representation.

currentState.focus: Verified the topological-invariance kernel of OQ-02.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED a verified kernel: created Hilbert13OQ02.lean (5 thm, 5 def, 0 axioms, 0 sorries) proving covering dimension is a topological invariant (covDimLE_homeo) and hence the 2n+1 KA superposition term count is presentation-independent (kaTermCount_invariant). Uses a universe-safe finite-cover + Set.ncard definition that compiles under Mathlib 4.26.0, unlike the companion Hilbert13GeneralSpaces.lean.
builtItems: covDimLE (universe-safe, Fin m covers) in Hilbert13OQ02.lean:62
insights: Covering dimension transports along any homeomorphism in both directions with NO compactness/metric assumption: push covers forward via e.symm, pull refinements back via e; order preserved exactly since x ∈ e⁻¹S ↔ e x ∈ S.

Since minimal KA term count = 2·dim+1 and dim is invariant, the superposition complexity is an invariant of the homeomorphism type — presentation-independent. This is the provable well-posedness kernel of the otherwise-fuzzy OQ-02.

Indexing finite covers by Fin m (Type 0) + Set.ncard order avoids the DecidablePred synthesis failure and universe-metavariable errors that stop the companion Hilbert13GeneralSpaces.lean from compiling.
mathlibGaps: Mathlib has no off-the-shelf Lebesgue covering dimension API used here; defined cleanly from scratch.
nextSteps: A Mechanic could repair Hilbert13GeneralSpaces.lean (DecidablePred in coverOrderAt; universe metavars in covDimLE/covDimEq).
The genuinely open part of OQ-02 — effective/efficient computation of a KA representation — remains; needs a computability model.
